subject.title: fix(ci): stop unrelated main updates from forcing PR rebases

question: Should OpenClaw adopt a non-strict coordinator merge rule backed by `openclaw/ci-gate` while retaining exact-merge enforcement for ordinary actors?
rationale: This changes the repository's server-enforced landing policy and failure boundary; tests can verify mechanics, but only maintainers can approve the intended coordinator trust model.

options.title: Adopt after complete proof
options.body: Fix the changelog-only verifier gap, demonstrate successful and failing hosted aggregate behavior, then enable the coordinator rule.

options.title: Retain exact-merge everywhere
options.body: Do not activate the non-strict coordinator path and continue rebasing contributor branches whenever `main` advances.

recommendation.title: Adopt after complete proof
recommendation.body: Fix the changelog-only verifier gap, demonstrate successful and failing hosted aggregate behavior, then enable the coordinator rule.

likelyOwner.reason: The linked design issue and implementation identify this person as the clearest available owner of the coordinator policy decision.
